newsitem.title: CANADA: Asia-Pacific lawmakers urge Korea peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Asia-Pacific lawmakers urge Korea peace talks.

text.p: Lawmakers from 22 countries including China and the United States on Friday urged South and North Korea to hold peace talks.

U.S. Representative Amory Houghton said the resolution adopted by the Asia Pacific Parliamentary Forum at its annual meeting was the first time all 22 countries had stated support for peace talks to include the two Koreas, China and the United States.
"I think that is a very specific and very helpful statement," Houghton, a Republican from New York, told a news conference.
The so-called "four party" talks were proposed by the United States and South Korea last April to North Korea and China.
The talks would seek to negotiate a lasting peace to replace the truce that ended the 1950-53 Korean War. China and North Korea have not formally responded to the invitation.

The resolution was part of a final communique issued by the parliamentary forum after a four-day annual meeting in Vancouver, Canada. The organisation groups legislators from 25 Pacifc Rim countries but three member states -- New Zealand, Laos and the Marshall Islands -- did not send delegations.

The resolution calls on South and North Korea to participate in four-party peace talks. It also urges them to "enhance mutual understanding and trust and solve problems between them in a peaceful manner."
The resolution was put forward by South Korea and the United States. North Korea is not a member of the forum.

The statement was unanimously passed by parliamentarians from Australia, Brunei, Cambodia, Canada, Chile, China, Fiji, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, Micronesia, Mongolia, Papua New Guinea, Peru, the Philippines, Russia, Singapore, Thailand, the United States and Vietnam.
